additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0443253-DC/Si-D/NZ-[ MP / P3 170000341]Charger has dropped offline on OCPP CRM:02681000617
additional_info.body:
Hey Liz,
Hope you are doing well.
It has been a very busy day at our end, I have just issued a reboot to that charger.
Will update you on its visibility to OCPP and SCB in a little while.
If you do head to site, it might be worth checking to see that failovers aren’t enabled by any chance on the routers.
We do note that the router is setup for ethernet and DHCP, so would be interesting to look upstream to see if the network device can see that port being active at all.
With Kind Regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0443253-DC/Si-D/NZ-[ MP / P3 170000341]Charger has dropped offline on OCPP CRM:02681000617
additional_info.body:
Hey Liz,
The charger has finished booting back up and is attempting to connect to the OCPP backend, but it is getting a 404 error (e.g. unable to find/access).
It also appears it is not getting an IP address from the upstream network.
I suggest next steps would be as stated below to check from the network router upstream to determine if it is seeing any attempts for connection or if the MAC address is visible.
Failing this, it might also be a physical connection issue outside of the charger.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd. Australia
Customer Services
Application Service Engineer
Phone: +61 499 701 794
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com

additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0443253-DC/Si-D/NZ-[ MP / P3 170000341]Charger has dropped offline on OCPP CRM:02681000617
additional_info.body:
Hi there,
Just touching base to let you know that we have successfully got charger 1 at Auckland airport back online.
The tech travelled to site and after trying multiple power cycles which didn’t work we looked at the upstream network connections as you suggested.
There didn’t seem to be any data crossing over the port that the charger was plugged into. The tech unplugged this and into a spare port, the lights started flashing and the charger came online on our back end. Right now , we are happy to say that it was a faulty network port but will monitor the charger closely.
Thanks a lot for your suggestion to look at this, really helped with our fault finding.
Cheers,
Liam Lubransky
Asset Management Technician
Asset Deployment & Operations
Meridian Energy Limited
New Zealand
M. 027 8399974
